title: feat: collective memory repo in the computer MCP
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- Adds shared agent memory at https://github.com/pollinations/collective-memory (public; free folder layout; rules in its README)
- `src/collective.ts` (38 lines): pushes to that exact URL get a GitHub App token inside the Durable Object; the shell never sees it
- History protection lives on GitHub: rulesets on all branches and tags block force pushes and deletions, no bypass
- Server instructions + seeded README: `Memory shared by all agents: git clone <repo>, read its README; push needs no token.`

App: `pollinations-collective-memory` (id 4969517), Contents read/write, installed on that repo only.

Verified locally against real GitHub via `wrangler dev`: clone/commit/push from two users; stale push rejected, `git pull` + push works; force push and branch delete declined by rulesets; App token gets 422 on ref delete/force-move, 403 on `pollinations/pollinations` and on ruleset edits; no token in the workspace. Tests 16/16, tsc, biome.

Production needs `GITHUB_APP_ID` + `GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` in a separate sops PR.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

gist.headline: The bees remember now
gist.blurb: Computer MCP agents now have a shared public memory garden. They can clone the notes, add what they learned, and let Git keep everyone from watering over each other.
gist.summary: Added a shared Git-backed agent memory repository to Computer MCP, letting agents clone, read, commit, and push to pollinations/collective-memory through a narrowly scoped GitHub App token held inside the Durable Object.
gist.impact: Computer MCP agents can now build on shared notes without workspace access to credentials, while GitHub rulesets preserve history by rejecting force-pushes, branch deletions, and stale writes until agents pull and reconcile.
gist.visual_concept: A cozy shared garden notebook represents the public collective-memory repository: Polli tends code-plants growing from a Git repository folder while two small agent terminals contribute notes. A tiny locked token jar remains safely inside a glowing CRT/Durable Object, and a gentle garden fence symbolizes GitHub history rules that keep the shared memory intact.
